nary_nodes.label: Incheon becomes world's busiest
evidence: South Korea's Incheon has become the world's busiest airport by international passenger traffic for the first time, new figures show.

Incheon International Airport, the main gateway to South Korea, served 38.4 million international passengers for the first six months of this year, according to preliminary data from the Airports Council International.

nary_nodes.label: Heathrow serves 37.79 million passengers
evidence: London Heathrow Airport ranked second with 37.79 million passengers, followed by Singapore's Changi Airport with 34.53 million.

nary_nodes.label: Dubai expected to fall outside top five
evidence: Dubai International Airport, which ranked second both in 2024 and 2025 based on full-year statistics, is expected to fall outside the top five this time.

nary_nodes.label: Heathrow and Incheon rank changes
evidence: London's Heathrow airport ranked fifth in 2024 and seventh in 2025, while Incheon ranked 12th and 13th, respectively.

nary_nodes.label: Passengers diverted from Middle East hubs
evidence: Incheon's airport attributed its rise partly to the diversion of passengers from aviation hubs in the Middle East because of the conflict between the US and Iran.

nary_nodes.label: Transfer passengers increase 18%
evidence: Some passengers who previously transited through Dubai on the way to Europe are now travelling via Incheon, the airport corporation said, fuelling an 18% rise in transfer passengers from the same period last year.

nary_nodes.label: Transfer passengers to Europe rise 63.2%
evidence: The number of transfer passengers whose final destinations were in Europe rose 63.2% to 210,000, it added.

nary_nodes.label: Infrastructure expansion enables larger traffic
evidence: The corporation said the expansion of infrastructure also enabled the airport to manage a larger traffic load.

nary_nodes.label: Incheon opened in 2001
evidence: Incheon, which opened in 2001, serves 158 international destinations.

nary_nodes.label: Kim expresses gratitude
evidence: "We're grateful for the [South Korean] government's support, the public's encouragement and the hard work of everyone stationed at the airport in making Incheon the world's No. 1 airport," said the Incheon airport corporation's acting president Kim Beom-ho.

nary_nodes.label: Kim plans to strengthen competitiveness
evidence: Kim added the corporation planned to strengthen competitiveness by focusing on passenger convenience.
